sources.placement: Where the decorative ball of a replayed swing is drawn. "address" keeps it at the address face, resting on the ground (#12955). "strike" moves it to where the face centre passes nearest that place around impact, so the drawn face meets the drawn ball (#15150, owner request 2026-11-20). Either way the ball is a display object: it is not measured, not simulated, and moving it changes no joint angle and no club dimension.
sources.search_window_s: Half width of the time window round the impact time in which the nearest pass of the face centre is looked for. 0.02 s is the window the impact-parameter extractor already uses for its swing plane (impact_parameters.extract.PLANE_WINDOW_S); at a driver head speed of about 45 m/s it spans about 0.9 m of travel each side.
sources.max_shift_m: Largest distance the ball may be moved from its address place. Beyond it the swing does not come back to the ball and moving the ball would hide a fault of the fit, so the address ball is kept and the reason is recorded. 0.15 m is a display judgement (about 3.5 ball diameters), not a measurement; the matched driver swing of 2026-11-20 needs about 0.10 m from the ground and 0.04 m from the address face centre.
sources.max_tee_height_m: Greatest height of the underside of the ball above the ground, by club head name; "default" serves every other club. Driver: 0.1016 m, the longest tee the Rules of Golf allow (Equipment Rules, Part 6: a tee must not be longer than 4 inches). It is an upper bound, not a typical tee: tour drivers are usually teed with the underside about 0.04 m up. Other clubs: 0, the ball lies on the ground. A ball held by a limit is no longer struck at the centre of the face; the placement record states by how much.
